liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One is relatively short but well played [10]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer considers this Candyman among the best they have heard [11]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The acoustic I Know You Rider is called gorgeous [15]
- Dark Star is relatively short but well played [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Rub**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- **Long Black Limousine**: rare: 4 archived performances [17]
- **Candyman/Equipment problems**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Stage Preparations**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Bill Graham Introduction/Six Days On The Road**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Cryptical Reprise**: rare: 9 archived performances [17]
- **New Minglewood Blues**: back after 119 archived shows (384 days) [17]
- **Ballad Of Casey JOnes**: rare: 3 archived performances [17]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Louisana Lady [17]

## The recordings

- **gd_nrps70-05-15.sbd.reynolds-kaplan.29473.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 67 songs; 420 min; rated 4.78/5 by 45 [1]
- **gd70-05-15.early-late.sbd.97.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 63 songs; 391 min; rated 4.76/5 by 95 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is surprisingly good, with the acoustic set especially enjoyable; Sound quality is described as nearly perfect [11][15]
- **gd1970-05-15.136575.late.aud.cooper.berger.flac16**: audience recording; 23 songs; 157 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has mic rustling and static on the first track; the cassette had been previously recorded on [3]
- **gd1970-05-15.136574.late.aud.cooper.berger.flac24**: audience recording; 23 songs; 157 min [4]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham [1]
- Show mixes electric Dead with porch-style acoustic folk and oldies, pointing toward the Dead's merged sound of the following year [7]
- Reviewer attended from fifth row center; the Dead and NRPS shared the bill. Suggests moving last two disc 2 tracks to separate early and late shows [8]
- Jerry and Bobby's banter between the acoustic songs is amusing [9]
- Reviewer praises Jerry's playing with the New Riders [14]
- Reviewer calls it legendary yet less known than the 5/2/70 and 2/13/70 shows [10]
- Once among the most widely circulated 1970 Dead shows, with 2/13-14/70 and 5/2/70, later issued as Dick's Picks 4 and 8 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd_nrps70-05-15.sbd.reynolds-kaplan.29473.shnf**: transferred by Chuck Reynolds and Seth Kaplan.; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Analog-to-digital transfer made from the master reels of the late show, including NRPS and acoustic and electric Dead sets [1]
- **gd70-05-15.early-late.sbd.97.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf, David Hollister, Jeff Tiedrich and David Finney; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1970-05-15.136575.late.aud.cooper.berger.flac16**: taped by Jim Cooper; transferred by Rob Berger; source: source: aud cassette master; taped by Jimmy Cooper; 2 hitachi mics > hitachi trq-222; nakamichi dragon > benchmark adc1 24/96 > mac > adobe audition cc >… [3]. Also: Late show audience recording, credited to Cooper and Berger, circulating as FLAC16 [3]
- **gd1970-05-15.136574.late.aud.cooper.berger.flac24**: taped by Jim Cooper; transferred by Rob Berger; source: source: aud cassette master; taped by Jimmy Cooper; 2 hitachi mics > hitachi trq-222; nakamichi dragon > benchmark adc1 24/96 > mac > adobe audition cc >… [4]
